requirements.summary: Baseline lsmod showed no usb_storage loaded (cmd-adc506d5f1d745d3). A blacklist+install /bin/false config was written (cmd-8e7c47e262834672) and confirmed present. Explicit modprobe usb-storage attempt failed via the install directive and lsmod confirmed the module was not inserted (cmd-c7f75b69d7d04654).

requirements.requirement: usb-storage module remains blocked after a reboot (persistence)
requirements.summary: Pre-reboot boot_id/uptime were captured (cmd-e443fd988b3349e8), a real reboot was issued and acknowledged (cmd-6e3deab9528a44f4), the node was observed unreachable during the transition (cmd-78595b13a28a4683, cmd-f67ea74e74634ef0), a new distinct boot_id/uptime confirmed the reboot completed (cmd-1606839fdfdc44f2), and post-reboot checks showed the config file still present, usb_storage absent from lsmod, and modprobe still blocked (cmd-ea505353772e424f). This directly demonstrates the full baseline->disruption->recovery transition required for a persistence claim.

requirements.requirement: Blocking mechanism is effective for early boot (initramfs) loading path, or confirmed unnecessary
requirements.summary: lsinitrd search confirmed usb_storage is not embedded in the current initramfs, so no dracut rebuild was needed for early-boot blocking; the modprobe.d blacklist/install directives are sufficient and were verified to persist and function after an actual reboot.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied the task contract: usb-storage was confirmed blocked immediately via a modprobe.d blacklist + install /bin/false directive, and this was re-verified as persistent across an actual observed reboot (distinct pre/post boot_id and uptime, an unreachable window during restart, and post-reboot confirmation that the config, lsmod state, and modprobe failure all held). Initramfs was checked and confirmed not to require rebuilding. Hygiene is clean aside from a trivial leftover log file from the backgrounded reboot command.
limitations: The /tmp/reboot.log residue from the backgrounded shutdown command was not explicitly cleaned up, though it is low-risk and does not affect the module-blacklist outcome.
Only one reboot cycle was captured; long-term durability beyond this single reboot cannot be directly observed from the evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor commands trace clearly to task outcomes: baseline check, config write, initramfs check, immediate verification, pre-reboot boot-identity capture, the reboot itself (required to prove the 'after reboot' contract), polling during the down window, and post-reboot re-verification. The only incidental residue is /tmp/reboot.log created by the backgrounded shutdown command (cmd-6e3deab9528a44f4), a small, low-risk log file that was not cleaned up; this is a minor, non-destructive leftover rather than a harmful or unnecessary mutation. No conflicting services, failed units, unsafe exposure, or package-state damage appeared in the after-executor snapshot.
